clue.text: Policeman at King's for the 20s

parts.note: a flic is French slang for a policeman
K is the abbreviation for king, with the possessive S kept

explanation.surface: A constable stationed at a King's establishment, dressed for the Roaring Twenties.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is a cross-reference to 20-across, the word for a film, so '20s' means films. 'for the' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Flicks is informal slang for films at the cinema, so it matches cinema showings.

clue.text: Covering body makes light of 20s

parts.note: a film is a thin covering layer
a star is a heavenly body

explanation.surface: Some protective wrapping makes light work of the Twenties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is the link word. A 'light' here is a leading figure, so a light of 20s (films) is a celebrated screen actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading light is a celebrity, and one shining in cinema is a famous screen actor.

clue.text: Liner fan may be damned

indicators.note: says the letters of the two words could be something else if rearranged

explanation.surface: A fan of ocean liners might be condemned to perdition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' tells you the letters of LINER and FAN can be shuffled into another word.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernal describes things belonging to hell, as damned souls do; both mean hellish or cursed.

clue.text: Piece of liturgy has Minogue changing sides

indicators.note: left swaps over to right, so the letter for left is exchanged for the letter for right

parts.note: Kylie Minogue is the Australian pop singer

explanation.surface: A church text in which the pop singer Kylie switches political allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords L is left and R is right; 'changing sides' swaps the L in KYLIE for an R.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kyrie eleison is a short prayer that forms part of the Christian Mass.

clue.text: Prunella, the player retaining part of part of play

indicators.note: one word holds another inside it, as a container keeps what it retains

parts.note: an actor is a player on stage

indicators.note: only a portion of the word is kept, with its first and last letters dropped

parts.note: a scene is a section of a play

explanation.surface: Prunella, the actress, keeps hold of a small role in the play.
explanation.walkthrough: Prunella looks like an actress's first name but is the genus name of the hedge-sparrow family. 'part of' trims the play section to its inner three letters, which 'retaining' holds inside the player.
explanation.definitionFit: Accentors are small songbirds such as the dunnock, classified in the genus Prunella.

clue.text: Playing Iago with parchment needed for 20s

definitions.note: describes a thing, the apparatus required to make or show films

indicators.note: playing about with the letters suggests rearranging them

explanation.surface: Performing Iago, with a parchment scroll as a necessary prop for the Twenties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' signals an anagram of IAGO plus PARCHMENT; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An early device for both shooting and projecting moving pictures, essential equipment for making films.

clue.text: Piece of liturgy seeking peace for both parts of island opposed

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland, one part of the island
NI is Northern Ireland, the other part of the island
con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A prayer for peace that both halves of Ireland are said to be against.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both parts of island' gives two pieces: the Republic and Northern Ireland. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An eirenicon is a proposal or text aimed at reconciliation, and the Orthodox liturgy has petitions for peace of that name.

clue.text: Modern 20 story about "Anna and the King of Siam"?

indicators.note: one word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a tale is a story
K is the abbreviation for king
in the musical The King and I, Anna is the I of the title

explanation.surface: A newfangled film tells the story of Anna and the King of Siam.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical 'The King and I' lets Anna stand for I, after K for the King; 'about' puts K and I inside TALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A talkie was a film with a soundtrack, the newest kind of film in the late 1920s.

clue.text: Writer Jean grips me as fair hair does

indicators.note: the writer's surname holds the next word inside it

parts.note: Jean Rhys was the author of Wide Sargasso Sea

explanation.surface: The novelist Jean holds me tight, the way blonde hair does.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb phrase: 'fair' and 'hair' end with the same sound, so fair does this with hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Two words whose endings sound alike are said to match in sound, which is the verb here.

clue.text: Lag back in the centre file

indicators.note: read the letters backwards
the answer is found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A convict goes back to the middle of the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the run REFIL inside 'centre file'; 'back' turns it round. 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lag is British slang for a convict, especially one serving a long or life sentence.

clue.text: Day when "Coloured" includes students of mixed breed

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday

indicators.note: the colour word takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: grey is a colour, so coloured grey
L is a learner, so two Ls are students

explanation.surface: A day when the word 'Coloured' covers pupils of mixed race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link; 'includes' puts the two learners inside the colour. 'Coloured' here just means a colour word.
explanation.definitionFit: Mongrelly is an adjective for something like a mongrel, a dog whose parentage is mixed.

clue.text: Poet painting in 20

parts.note: Andrew Motion was UK Poet Laureate
a painting is a picture

explanation.surface: A poet's painting appears in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word between the wordplay and the cross-reference to 20-across (a film).
explanation.definitionFit: A motion picture is the formal name for a film shown in the cinema.

clue.text: Strawberry grower has topless thing to wear in addition

indicators.note: the trimmed piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a sum is an addition

indicators.note: the first letter is removed

parts.note: a garment is an item of clothing

explanation.surface: A strawberry farmer also owns a skimpy item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the first letter from the clothing word, and 'in' puts what is left inside the addition. A strawberry spreads by runners. 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarmentum is a runner, the creeping stem by which a strawberry plant spreads.

clue.text: Setter coming in to investigate what made 20s 7s?

indicators.note: the setter goes inside the next piece

parts.note: to nose is to pry or investigate
the setter refers to themselves as I

explanation.surface: The setter arrives to look into what turned silent films into talkies.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is MOVIE and 7 is TALKIE: sound turned films into talkies.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound, loosely called noise, is what turned silent films into talking pictures.

clue.text: Weird goings-on about a king of Thebes in Greek poems

indicators.note: the first word wraps around what follows

parts.note: antics are odd or silly goings-on
Creon was king of Thebes in Greek tragedy

explanation.surface: Strange behaviour surrounding a Theban monarch in Greek verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the goings-on around the king with A in front. Creon appears in Sophocles' Theban plays. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Anacreontics are verses in the style of Anacreon, the ancient Greek lyric poet.

clue.text: Old show for old king (not original) from 57 to 71 in the table

parts.note: a raree show was an old travelling peep show

indicators.note: the following word is removed

parts.note: Arthur is the legendary early king of Britain
ur- is a prefix meaning original or earliest

explanation.surface: An antique show stands in for a former monarch, part of the periodic table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes UR (from 'original', as in ur-text) from ARTHUR, leaving ARTH. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The lanthanide elements, atomic numbers 57 to 71 in the periodic table, are known as rare earths.

clue.text: Oboe is politically correct in arrangement for the 20s

definitions.note: describes a place to see films, an early cinema

indicators.note: arranging means placing in a new order

explanation.surface: An oboe arranged in a politically sensitive way for the Twenties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in arrangement' rearranges OBOEIS plus PC. The definition describes a place for films.
explanation.definitionFit: Bioscope was an early name for a cinema or film projector, still used in South Africa for the cinema.

clue.text: Way to further incite fish

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
to urge on is to encourage further

explanation.surface: How to stir up a fish even more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sturgeon is a large fish, famous as the source of caviar.

clue.text: Heathen princess embraced by racing driver and spin doctor

indicators.note: the first pieces are held inside the following one

parts.note: Alain Prost is a French racing driver
a pagan is a heathen
Di is Princess Diana

explanation.surface: A pagan princess is hugged by a Formula One driver and a press adviser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced by' puts the heathen and the princess inside the four-time Formula One champion's name. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A propagandist pushes a slanted message, which is exactly a political spin doctor's job.

clue.text: A fiend and a half are going to take place

parts.note: an imp is a small devil or fiend
an end is one half of a sports pitch, which teams swap at half-time

explanation.surface: A devil and a half are on their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link. Each team defends one end, or half, of a pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Events that impend are about to happen, hanging over us in the near future.

clue.text: Head and feet removed from king who played lyre with zest

indicators.note: the first letter of the first word and the last letters of the second are taken away

parts.note: King David played the lyre in the Bible

explanation.surface: A beheaded king who played the lyre enthusiastically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head and feet removed from' drops D from the front of DAVID and RE from the end of LYRE, leaving AVID and LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Avidly means eagerly and keenly, with real enthusiasm and gusto.

clue.text: Little time to struggle in celluloid

parts.note: mo is short for moment
to vie is to compete or struggle

explanation.surface: A brief moment spent fighting on film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Celluloid was the material of film stock, so it stands by extension for films themselves.

clue.text: Smacker from singer drinking wines

indicators.note: the singer takes the wines inside

parts.note: Cher is the American pop singer
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine, so Astis are wines

explanation.surface: Someone who spanks, taken from a singer downing wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chastiser punishes, and a smacker hits someone as punishment.

clue.text: Subject to 20?

parts.note: 20-across is a film, and a pic is a film

explanation.surface: Subject to the movies?
explanation.walkthrough: 20 refers to 20-across, MOVIE; 'pic' is informal for a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the subject of a discussion or piece of writing.

clue.text: George I makes provision for home-made wines

definitions.meaning: George Bush senior, the first of two President George Bushes
a plant whose flowers and berries are made into country wines at home

explanation.surface: King George I lays in a supply of home brews.
explanation.walkthrough: George I looks like the Hanoverian king, but the first George Bush, father of George W, is Bush the elder.
explanation.definitionFit: The first President George Bush is known as Bush the elder, and the elder shrub gives elderflower and elderberry wine.

clue.text: Take into gym to investigate

indicators.note: the first word goes inside the next

parts.note: PE is physical education, gym class
to rob is to take

explanation.surface: Bring something into the gym to look into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To probe is to explore or examine closely, which is to investigate.

clue.text: Tuesday or Wednesday for the ready-made

indicators.note: the letters are made into something else

explanation.surface: A weekday for off-the-peg goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready-made' hides the anagram: THEREADY made into new order. Counting from Sunday or Monday, the third day is Tuesday or Wednesday.
explanation.definitionFit: The third day of the week is Tuesday if the week starts Sunday, Wednesday if it starts Monday.

clue.text: Investigate the 20s

definitions.meaning: to vet or check someone carefully
the films, the cinema as a medium

explanation.definitionFit: To screen is to vet, and the screen means the cinema world of films.
